ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, lines $AB$ and $CD$ intersect at point $O$, $EO\perp CD$ at point $O$, and $OF$ bisects $\angle BOC$. If $\angle AOC = 58^\circ$, what is the degree measure of $\angle EOF$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} From the construction, we have\\
$\because \angle AOC + \angle BOC = 180^\circ$, $\angle AOC = 58^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle BOC = 122^\circ$,\\
$\because OF$ bisects $\angle BOC$,\\
$\therefore \angle COF = \frac{1}{2}\angle BOC = 61^\circ$,\\
$\because EO \perp CD$,\\
$\therefore \angle COE = 90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle EOF = \angle COE - \angle COF = 90^\circ - 61^\circ = \boxed{29^\circ}$;

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, point O is on the horizontal straight line AB; OA points to the left, OB points to the right, and they are opposite rays. Another straight line CD passes through O; OC points to the upper left, and OD points to the lower right. OE extends from O toward the upper right relatively gently, and OF extends from O toward the upper right relatively steeply; OF is located between OC and OE. In the figure, there is a right-angle mark near OC and OE, corresponding to EO being perpendicular to CD. Reasoning: From the image it can be seen that OA and OB are opposite rays, and OC is on another intersecting straight line, so ∠AOC and ∠BOC form a pair of adjacent supplementary angles, with a sum of 180°. It is known that ∠AOC = 58°, therefore ∠BOC = 180° - 58° = 122°. Also because OF bisects ∠BOC, ∠COF = 122° ÷ 2 = 61°. Since EO ⟂ CD, and OC is on straight line CD, ∠COE = 90°. In the figure, OF is between OC and OE, therefore ∠EOF = ∠COE - ∠COF = 90° - 61° = 29°.
